blocks.text: Brackenridge Civil Group Inc is a civil engineering firm in the county seat, and it has done the same plain work since it was founded in 1996. We design the site work that has to be built before anything above it can stand: grading, drainage, roadways, and the utilities that run beneath them. Our clients are the public bodies and private builders who put up work in this part of the county, among them municipal public works departments, a regional water authority, and private developers. This overview sets out what the firm does, how it runs a job, and shows the work through a handful of past projects. It is written to claim only what is true.

Civil design touches the ground and everything set into it, and the firm's lines of work follow from that. We grade sites so they sit and drain as they must, and we prepare the erosion and sediment control that holds the soil while it is open. We design stormwater management, from the drainage study that stands behind a plan through the pipes, inlets, and detention that carry runoff off a site within the county's standards. We lay out roadways, whether a new street in a subdivision or the widening and resurfacing of an existing one, and we design the water, sanitary sewer, and storm utilities that go with them. On a subdivision these arrive as one coordinated set. On a public works job they may come one line at a time, as the program and the budget allow. A single drainage complaint at one intersection may need only a study and a modest fix, and it has the same claim on our care as a full subdivision.

The firm keeps one order of work and does not vary it. A job begins with a walk of the site and a scope set down in writing, so the client and the firm agree on the work before it starts. The design is done at our own boards and checked before it is issued. Nothing leaves this office until the set has been reviewed and the cover sheet sealed, and that order holds on every job without exception. The drawings and specifications we prepare are made to be built from and to carry a contractor and a reviewer through the work without guesswork. The practice is small, small enough that the same hand reaches every job and steady enough to keep several moving at once.

A good part of the firm's work is done for public bodies, and it is prepared to their standards and their review. We take a set through the county's drainage and roadway review, prepare the permit documents a job requires, and answer the comments that come back until the set is approved. The paperwork is kept as carefully as the drawings. An executed agreement is logged when it returns to the office, scanned, and filed with the plans it belongs to, so that a project folder holds the whole record of a job and not merely its sheets. Public work runs on that kind of order, and the firm is built for it.

A few past projects, drawn from across the last several years, give a fair sense of the work. For {{fact:f:E-2001-001.client}} we carried the site grading and stormwater design from the first walk of the ground through the county's review. For {{fact:f:E-2004-001.client}} we handled the roadway and utility design and saw the set through approval. For {{fact:f:E-2005-001.client}} we prepared a drainage study and designed the improvements that followed from it. For {{fact:f:E-2006-001.client}} we designed the grading and utilities for a site the client was preparing to build. For {{fact:f:E-2007-001.client}} we are carrying the stormwater and roadway design now. These are offered as examples of the kind of project the firm takes on, not as a list of our clients or a measure of the firm's book of business, and we do not, as a matter of practice, discuss one client's engagement with another.

If you have a site that needs civil design, begin with a conversation and a look at the ground. Direct inquiries to Mark Todd, Principal Engineer, who will walk the site and set a scope in writing before any work is undertaken.
